scenario: An export-promotion newsletter features only textile exporters that remain active for three years and post annual export-growth above 40%. A trade analyst uses the newsletter average to estimate typical growth across all exporters.

data.description: Only exporters with growth above 40 percentage points and enough survivorship are included. Growth is modeled as Normal with known standard deviation sigma = 25 percentage points.

question: Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean annual export-growth rate mu across all exporters, and (b) the fraction of exporters that appear in the newsletter.
naive_answer: Typical exporter growth is about 52 percentage points because that is the newsletter average.
naive_trap: The newsletter features only upper-tail survivors, not the full exporter base.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: Solve 52.13 = mu + 25*lambda((40-mu)/25). Step 2: The solution has alpha about 1.2, so mu = 40 - 1.2*25 = 10. Step 3: The featured fraction is sf(1.2) = 0.1151.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(40-mu)/25
    return mu + 25*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a) - 52.13
mu=brentq(eq,-100,39.99)
frac=norm.sf((40-mu)/25)
assert abs(mu-10) < 1 and abs(frac-0.1151) < 0.005
